title: 8th-Grade Math: From Numbers to Lines, Shapes and Data
length_note: The course has 36 classes and runs about 1,155 minutes, or roughly 19 hours. US 8th-grade math covers five big strands: the number system, exponents, linear relationships and functions, geometry, and data. I gave each a separate set of classes so nothing is skipped and no class is crowded. Most classes are 30 minutes, as requested. Classes that combine several steps, such as elimination, dilations, cones and spheres, and lines of fit, run 35 minutes. The final review runs 45 minutes. Each class has worked examples and practice questions that explain the reasoning in the 'why'. The order is: numbers, exponents, slope and linear equations, functions, systems, transformations and angles, Pythagorean theorem, volume, data. Each stage uses the one before it. Classes marked needs_research use real-world numbers or data sets that must be checked and sourced before the lesson is written.

classes.title: Rational Numbers and Their Decimals
classes.goal: Turn a fraction into a decimal, and a repeating decimal back into a fraction, and explain why the decimal either stops or repeats.
topics: What counts as a rational number
Long division to find decimal forms
Writing a repeating decimal as a fraction

classes.title: Irrational Numbers and Roots
classes.goal: Say what makes a number irrational and tell rational from irrational numbers, including square roots of non-perfect squares and pi.
topics: Why some decimals never end and never repeat
Sorting numbers into rational and irrational

classes.title: Estimating and Ordering Irrational Numbers
classes.goal: Estimate an irrational number such as √20 and place it on a number line next to other rational and irrational numbers.
topics: Bounding a root between two whole numbers
Refining an estimate to tenths and hundredths
Placing values on a number line

classes.title: Exponent Rules for Whole Numbers
classes.goal: Simplify expressions using the product, quotient and power rules, and explain each rule by expanding the powers.

classes.title: Zero and Negative Exponents
classes.goal: Evaluate and simplify expressions with zero and negative exponents, and explain why they are defined the way they are.
topics: Why a number to the power 0 equals 1
Extending the exponent rules to all integers

classes.title: Solving with Squares and Cubes
classes.goal: Solve equations like x² = 49 and x³ = 27, and state when there are two answers and when there is one.
topics: Square root and cube root as undoing a power
Equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p

classes.title: Scientific Notation: Reading and Writing
classes.goal: Write very large and very small numbers in scientific notation and convert back to standard form.
topics: Positive and negative powers for big and small numbers
Why the first factor is between 1 and 10

classes.title: Scientific Notation: Comparing and Calculating
classes.goal: Compare, multiply and divide numbers in scientific notation, and say how many times larger one quantity is than another.
topics: Multiplying and dividing in scientific notation
Real-world quantities such as distances, sizes and populations

classes.title: Proportional Relationships and Unit Rate
classes.goal: Find the unit rate in a proportional relationship and compare two proportional relationships shown in different ways.
topics: Unit rate from a table, graph or equation

classes.title: Slope
classes.goal: Find the slope of a line from a graph or two points, and explain slope as rise over run using similar triangles.
topics: Positive, negative, zero and undefined slope
Why slope is the same anywhere on a line

classes.title: Lines: y = mx and y = mx + b
classes.goal: Write and graph the equation of a line from its slope and y-intercept, and read both from a graph.
topics: The y-intercept as the starting value
Writing an equation from a graph

classes.title: Solving Linear Equations in One Variable
classes.goal: Solve multi-step equations, including ones with the distributive property and fractions, and check the answer.

classes.title: Variables on Both Sides: One, None or Infinitely Many Solutions
classes.goal: Solve equations with variables on both sides and tell whether they have one solution, no solution or infinitely many.
topics: Reading the result: x = number, false statement, true statement
Why no solution and infinite solutions happen
Writing an equation with a given number of solutions

classes.title: What Is a Function?
classes.goal: Say what a function is and decide whether a relation is a function by checking each input has exactly one output.
topics: Function or not, from tables, mappings and graphs

classes.title: Four Ways to Show a Function
classes.goal: Move between a function's words, table, graph and equation.
topics: Function rules in words and equations

classes.title: Linear and Nonlinear Functions
classes.goal: Tell linear from nonlinear functions using a table, graph or equation, and explain what a constant rate of change looks like.
topics: y = mx + b as the linear form
Examples of nonlinear functions, such as area of a square

classes.title: Modeling with Linear Functions
classes.goal: Build a linear function from a situation, say what the rate of change and starting value mean, and describe a graph as a story.
topics: Finding slope and intercept from two data points
Meaning of rate of change and initial value in context
Sketching a graph from a description
Describing increasing, decreasing and constant sections

classes.title: Comparing Two Functions
classes.goal: Compare two functions given in different forms and say which has the greater rate of change or starting value.
topics: Comparing a table with an equation
Comparing a graph with a description

classes.title: Systems of Equations by Graphing
classes.goal: Explain that the solution of a system is where the lines cross, and say when there is one, none or infinitely many.
topics: Two equations, one pair of variables
Checking a solution in both equations

classes.title: Systems by Substitution
classes.goal: Solve a system by substituting one equation into the other, and check the result.
topics: Back-substituting to find the second variable

classes.title: Systems by Elimination
classes.goal: Solve a system by adding or subtracting equations, multiplying first when needed, and choose between elimination and substitution.
topics: Adding equations to cancel a variable
Multiplying an equation to make matching coefficients

classes.title: Systems in the Real World
classes.goal: Turn a word problem into a system, solve it, and say what the answer means in the situation.
topics: Writing two equations from a story
Checking that the answer makes sense

classes.title: Rigid Motions: Translations, Reflections and Rotations
classes.goal: Describe and perform a translation, reflection or rotation and say what stays the same when a figure moves.

classes.title: Transformations on the Coordinate Plane
classes.goal: Find the new coordinates of a point or shape after a translation, reflection or rotation.
topics: Reflection over the x-axis and y-axis
Rotations of 90°, 180° and 270° about the origin
Writing a rule for what happened to the points

classes.title: Congruent Figures
classes.goal: Show two figures are congruent by describing a sequence of rigid motions that maps one onto the other.
topics: Explaining why two figures are or are not congruent

classes.title: Dilations and Similar Figures
classes.goal: Enlarge or shrink a figure using a scale factor, and show two figures are similar using dilations and rigid motions.
topics: Similar figures: same shape, proportional sides, equal angles

classes.title: Angles in Triangles and with Parallel Lines
classes.goal: Use the triangle angle sum and the angle pairs formed by a transversal to find missing angles and give reasons.
topics: Corresponding, alternate interior and vertical angles

classes.title: The Pythagorean Theorem: Why It Works
classes.goal: State the theorem and explain it with squares on the sides of a right triangle.

classes.title: Using the Pythagorean Theorem and Its Converse
classes.goal: Find a missing leg, and test whether a triangle with three given sides is a right triangle.
topics: Choosing the right form of the equation

classes.title: Distance and Real-World Right Triangles
classes.goal: Find the distance between two points on a coordinate plane and solve real problems such as ladders, diagonals and shortest paths.
topics: Drawing a right triangle between two points

classes.title: Volume of Cylinders
classes.goal: Find the volume of a cylinder and explain it as area of the base times height.
topics: Working backward from volume to radius or height

classes.title: Volume of Cones and Spheres
classes.goal: Find the volume of cones and spheres and compare them with cylinders, including the one-third relationship.
topics: Cone as one-third of a cylinder with the same base and height
Leaving answers in terms of pi or rounding

classes.title: Scatter Plots and Patterns
classes.goal: Make a scatter plot and describe the pattern, including clusters, outliers, and positive, negative or no association.
topics: Association is not the same as cause

classes.title: Lines of Best Fit
classes.goal: Draw an informal line of fit, write its equation, and use it to make predictions.
topics: Drawing a line close to most points
Choosing two points to find the slope
Writing y = mx + b for the data
Predicting, and the limits of predicting

classes.title: Two-Way Tables
classes.goal: Read and build a two-way table and use relative frequencies to describe a link between two categories.
topics: Deciding whether two categories seem related

classes.title: Course Review and Mixed Practice
classes.goal: Choose the right idea from the course for a mixed problem and explain the choice.
topics: Spotting which tool a question needs
Looking back at the toughest ideas
